answer: Hold payout on any application without verified income until a lending team leader verifies it, until the app makes the check mandatory, then review past loans without one: [F3] of sampled loans had no verified income, and those loans are in arrears far more often.
exec_summary: [F2] of [F1] sampled loans had no income verification, [F3] of the sample.
[F5] of those loans are in arrears, against [F8] of loans with a check.
At about [F9] loans a month, that rate means about [F10] new loans a month without a check.
Holding only those applications keeps the checks with lending team leaders and leaves the two compliance staff free to review past loans.
situation: An online lender whose rules and policy require verified income on every loan.
complication: Staff can skip the income check, and many sampled loans have none.
key_question: Does the lender meet the verified-income requirement, and what must change?

titles.situation: The lender's income checks have a gap.
titles.options: Two ways to close the gap until the app changes.
titles.recommendation: Flag skipped checks now and make the field mandatory.
titles.roadmap: Stop new gaps first, then review past loans.
titles.kpis: Two measures show the gap is closed.
titles.risks: The main risk is customers harmed by unaffordable loans.
